Install zlocale@0.0.3 . Use zlocale in browser/server/shared code, zlocale/node only on Node, and zlocale/zyro when connecting reactive UI. This guide describes application integration. Installing the package does not automatically add a framework-managed i18n service, negotiate Accept-Language or build localized routes.

Keep language and country separate: a language choice is not a currency, tax jurisdiction or user timezone. Use precise BCP-47 tags such as fr-CA when the site actually has regional behavior. Catalog lookup can fall back to parent locales, while the async locale controller expects explicit catalogs for the chosen base locale. If you support fr-CA , either provide its controller manifest entry or design an explicit host loader that supplies the correct base catalog; do not assume it automatically imports fr . Validate settings once at startup. createI18n validates canonical locale and timezone syntax, but the host must also ensure the default is supported, settings are nonempty/bounded and all required domain catalogs exist. Dynamic settings loaded from a database need runtime validation before they replace the current policy; a TypeScript interface alone is insufficient.
Include application settings in zerux.config.js or zerux.config.ts

appLanguage here is a custom application-owned namespace. ZeruxJS allows custom config fields, but neither the framework bootstrap nor zlocale consumes this key automatically. Your plugin reads it, validates it, preloads catalogs and creates the translator. This keeps the setting alongside DB/cache configuration without pretending it is a built-in service option. For an ESM zerux.config.js , use the same object with a JavaScript settings module and / @type {import('zeruxjs').ZeruxConfig & {appLanguage: import('./language-settings.js').SiteLanguageSettings}} / where your settings module exports the corresponding JSDoc type. Keep one active config file. Do not put private profile data or credentials in these public language settings, or serialize the whole framework config to the browser.
Preload the server's active catalog set

For a small site, import these catalogs at startup. For large catalogs, use createCatalogLoader with literal allowlisted imports, then explicitly preload the hot locale/domain combinations before the server accepts requests. Module catalogs such as fr/acme-cart belong in the same host-owned loading plan. Choose a catalog capacity for locales times domains; the default registry holds at most 64 catalogs. The registry and native Intl formatter cache are application-owned and bounded. Translation calls perform no filesystem/network I/O. For rarely visited locales, warm catalogs in deployment/background work or use an explicit prepared route boundary; do not hide a cold disk read in every translation or request. A loader cache and an i18n registry are separate owners: clearing one does not evict the other automatically.
Register a request-safe ZeruxJS site plugin

This example uses a small, preloaded public catalog set and a ?lang= policy. It stores a locale-fixed translator in request state so routes/modules do not mutate a shared language. The named middleware is explicitly attached to the route. The config example and settings module intentionally reference the same exported policy. If settings come from api.getConfig().appLanguage instead, treat that value as unknown, validate it at registration and pass the validated result into the same factory. api.setComposable can expose an application-owned translator facade to other routes; it is distinct from api.service , whose managed service names are fixed by the framework. Do not call i18n.setLocale per request on this shared owner. forLocale avoids mutable request state entirely. If deeply nested server code needs ambient request lookup, use createRequestI18n from zlocale/node and wrap the actual awaited downstream handler with run(locale, next) ; its AsyncLocalStorage context isolates concurrent requests. The host owns its dispose() after in-flight work finishes. Do not return an arbitrary disposer from plugin registration and assume the framework invokes it; use a managed worker/lifecycle
Choose language precedence and persistence deliberately

A practical policy is explicit localized URL, then authenticated saved preference, then validated cookie, then an explicitly negotiated Accept-Language value, then the site default. This ordering is a site policy, not implemented automatically by zlocale. The minimal example above only reads ?lang= and falls back to the default. It does not claim to parse Accept-Language weights or authenticate a profile preference. Never concatenate a preference into a file path or import expression. Invalid/unsupported choices should fall back or receive a deliberate 400 response; a supported locale is not a permission to access another tenant's settings. Save authenticated profile preferences through your normal authorization/CSRF policy. Browser storage is optional UI convenience, untrusted on read and unavailable to the server. A public language preference cookie is not an authentication cookie; choose cookie path/lifetime/SameSite/Secure policy in the host. For public SEO pages, locale-specific URLs such as /fr/about make links shareable and cache keys explicit. The application must create those routes, canonical URLs and hreflang links; zlocale does not do it. Content-Language does not creat

Provide labels in each language, a persistent visible field label and a status region. The host chooses how its bundled application obtains the initial server-selected locale and public catalogs. Initialize the first locale/catalogs before the first render, or hydrate the public server snapshot described below. The example's English status text is illustrative; a complete UI translates its own loading/error/accessibility messages too. If modules contribute domains, add those manifest imports and include the domains in the controller's required set. Every selected locale must provide that complete set. A failed current load leaves the previous locale active; obsolete selections resolve false. Do not persist a preference until it successfully applies. If you use localStorage, catch access/storage errors and validate stored values against the same allowlist. The controller changes translation state. A UI must also render reactively: use createZyroI18n(i18n, signal) and call its methods inside reactive children, or subscribe with another renderer. Setting <html lang alone does not translate existing DOM text. For RTL layouts use CSS logical properties and deliberate directional icons;

On the server, serializeCatalogs(publicPageCatalogs) produces an HTML-safe JSON data-block payload. Send only the public locale/domain subset the page requires. On the client, read that block's textContent , call parseCatalogs , and pass its catalogs to createI18n before mounting. Keep the same selected locale, timezone and fallback settings on both sides. Do not refetch the same catalogs just to reconstruct server-rendered text. Use a non-executable script[type="application/json"] data block, never eval or raw string interpolation into a JavaScript program. Escaping prevents HTML script breakout; it does not remove confidential data. Do not serialize database configuration, a profile object, cookies, tokens or an entire request. Formatting can differ across ICU/CLDR deployments; test the actual server/browser versions when exact hydration text matters.

Use a separate catalog/settings owner for each tenant/runtime boundary when settings or private translations differ. Shared immutable public catalogs may be reused, but a global mutable site locale is unsafe. Background jobs receive a saved validated locale and use a fixed translator, rather than expecting an HTTP request context to exist. Load only a tenant's explicitly approved domains. Verify the default and every supported locale, missing-message fallback, plural counts, regional tags, UTC/user timezone choices, concurrent requests and rapid browser selections. Test a rejected locale chunk, private/shared-cache isolation, accessible language control, RTL text/layout and host teardown. Record missing catalog/deployment failures without logging private translated messages or profile values. A browser-only locale change does not persist a server preference unless the application explicitly saves it.

A plugin exports a default registration function (register and plugin are also recognized). Plugins run during runtime creation. The optional application entry module can register additional resources.

The API registers and removes routes, middleware and workers; sets controllers and composables; reads config and structure; exposes services, protocols, template variables and load metrics. See API reference for exported runtime interfaces.

Development stages a replacement runtime before activation. A failed rebuild or worker startup leaves the last activated runtime serving. Return cleanup functions from startup workers and release resources owned by the previous generation.

A plugin is startup code, not request middleware. Register routes, middleware and owned workers through the supplied API, then let the runtime create handlers. Do not open a process-global connection that survives reload unless a separate owner deliberately manages that lifetime. A generic service type is a compile-time description, not a cast that starts a missing service. Configure cache in the application first; handle disabled/degraded state instead of assuming non-null. A public health response should not expose connection URLs, keys or detailed internal errors.

Plugin code can read api.getConfig and api.getStructure. Service bootstrap removes sensitive raw service options before public runtime config is exposed; do not keep an unsanitized config singleton and return it from a route. If a package has no managed startup key, create its resource in an explicit plugin/worker owner rather than inventing a magic top-level setting. Use api.variables for controlled template-variable registration and api.protocols for registered gateway methods. Those APIs have their own validation, authorization and cleanup contracts. A route prefix or protocol name is not a sandbox for plugin code.

Stage the replacement generation without destroying the active one on preparation failure. Startup workers can return cleanup; ordinary plugin registration is not documented as an arbitrary returned-disposer lifecycle. Use the worker/service owner for handles and test that failed startup closes resources already created. Test duplicate route registration, overlapping service routes, disabled dependencies and an unsuccessful reload while an old request is still running. Verify that an optional integration failure is visible as degraded/disabled state rather than an apparently successful registration. See [plugin API](plugin-reference.md) for the exact methods and [service lifecycle](service-lifecycle.md) for reverse-order cleanup.

Publish domain-isolated locale catalogs and receive the host-selected translator instead of owning a global language. The [module/plugin translation guide](localization-package-authoring.md) explains packaging, explicit imports and typed route integration. The [site language guide](localization-site-settings.md) covers host settings and request isolation.

Startup workers run after bootstrap and before HTTP requests are accepted. A handler receives runtime, mode, config, structure, logger, env and state. Return cleanup for intervals, queues and sockets.

defineThreadWorker(name, script, options) describes a Node worker_threads pool. Register it with api.addThreadWorker, retrieve it with api.getThreadWorker and await pool.run(payload). The worker module exports a function. Configure sensible minThreads and maxThreads for the deployment CPU budget.
Reload and shutdown stop pools and run worker cleanup. Keep tasks bounded and account for rejection when a pool shuts down. Do not use CPU worker pools as a substitute for a durable job queue.
Match ownership to the kind of work

A lifecycle worker starts with a runtime generation and returns cleanup. A thread worker executes CPU-oriented tasks with explicit pool limits. A queue worker consumes durable Redis jobs with retry/idempotency semantics. Do not use a module-level interval as an undocumented substitute for any of these owners. Configure worker.minThreads/maxThreads for thread defaults; configure queue.workers separately for BullMQ processors. Each replica multiplies the configured concurrency. A process-local memory map or semaphore cannot enforce a deployment-wide rate limit.

Use defineWorker/defineThreadWorker and exported context types. Keep task inputs serializable and validate unknown request fields before starting work. A task result type does not make a multi-operation database action atomic. Preserve cancellation and distinguish an intentional abort from a retryable infrastructure failure. Test worker startup failure before activation, cleanup after a later resource fails, shutdown with in-flight work and replacement generation startup. The old active runtime should not be discarded merely because preparing a replacement failed. Ensure all owned timers/subscriptions release even when one cleanup rejects.

Observe queue lag, thread memory and downstream capacity rather than maximizing counts blindly. CPU work can block event-loop progress and prevent queue lock renewal; move it to the correct worker strategy. For external effects such as mail/payment, persist idempotency and ambiguous outcomes so a retried task does not repeat an irreversible action.

Model Use --- --- Startup worker Start/stop background resources with the runtime Thread pool CPU-bound work isolated in worker_threads Redis job queue Durable scheduling/retries across processes and restarts A thread pool has no durable job journal. A startup interval has no cross-replica election. Select the model by the delivery and ownership contract, not only by whether a task runs in the background.
The script path resolves relative to the application root unless absolute or a file URL. The module exports default, handler, process or run. Define a pure task where possible:

Retrieve the pool through the plugin API or runtime plugin adapter and await run(payload). Handle missing registration and rejection. Payload/result values cross Node's structured-clone boundary; do not send sockets, service managers or request contexts.

The generic compiler source roots do not automatically include an arbitrary workers directory. Ship or compile the referenced worker module explicitly, and verify the path in the production artifact. A successful route build does not prove an external worker script exists. A JavaScript worker can be deployed directly; TypeScript workers depend on the appropriate loader/source availability.

Set thread limits for the container's CPU and memory budget. More threads can increase contention, not throughput. Pools stop during generation cleanup and pending/running tasks can reject on shutdown. Use durable queue work when a process crash must not lose the task.

@zeruxjs/db provides the shared database layer. Adapter packages cover MongoDB, MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQLite, with db-sql-core shared by SQL adapters. Configure named connections and an explicit default rather than embedding credentials in handlers.

The cache configuration selects a connector, options, prefix and default TTL. cache-redis supplies Redis integration. Startup timeout and required control whether missing cache infrastructure blocks startup.

Optional files, email, analytics, tags, reports and queue configurations initialize generation-scoped managers. Plugins access api.service(name); handlers access context.services.get(name). Service methods belong to their package APIs.

Database and cache initialize before dependent managers. Resources close in reverse initialization order after prior requests finish. Analytics is best effort; email tracking is opt-in. Use queue workers for durable asynchronous jobs and thread workers for CPU work.
Select one owner for each manager

Framework configuration creates generation-owned managers. Standalone factories create caller-owned managers. Do not configure one manager in zerux.config.js and create another pool in every route. In plugins use api.service; request service lookup returns an unknown-shaped value that must be checked and used with the real package contract. The type argument does not prove the manager exists. Choose whether a dependency is required during startup, then make request behavior consistent with disabled/degraded state. Health endpoints should summarize readiness without exposing private settings.

Read the dedicated chapters for [database](configuration-database.md), [cache](configuration-cache.md), [files](configuration-files.md), [email](configuration-email.md), [analytics](configuration-analytics.md), [tags](configuration-tags.md), [reports](configuration-reports.md) and [queue](configuration-queue.md). They distinguish runtime keys from standalone options and document callback dependencies. A package without a managed startup key remains usable: instantiate it in the appropriate plugin, worker or browser component. Unknown root config properties do not trigger automatic initialization. Authentication/security helpers require explicit application enforcement rather than an empty auth/security object.

Initialization order follows dependencies, while shutdown drains owned resources in reverse order. Database failures and required cache/queue failures differ from best-effort analytics or optional dashboards. Test these policies deliberately instead of treating every outage as either universally fatal or silently ignored. Keep a manager alive while its generation is serving requests, then release it at the generation boundary. Closing it in a request finally block can break simultaneous users. A static docs export does not start these services and cannot validate external database/SMTP/Redis behavior.
cached(payload, policy) can set visibility, maxAge, ETag and Vary. A public cache policy must never be applied to personalized data. context.setCache sets policy directly.
stream(source, options) accepts a bounded stream source and handles backpressure and client disconnects. Streaming responses use no-store, no-transform. Set contentType and maxBytes deliberately.
For route.meta.streamBody, consume requestStream incrementally, track total bytes and reject excess input. Do not first accumulate the whole request into memory.

A response cache policy answers who may reuse a representation and for how long. A manager cache stores application values; it does not by itself configure HTTP headers. Keep authenticated and public responses separate, and do not reuse a public cache key for user-specific content. The precise cache policy names are versioned API; use the exported type and the [response reference](response-reference.md) before adapting this pattern. Conditional requests and an ETag still need the same authorization check as an uncached request. Never let an If-None-Match shortcut reveal the existence of another tenant's private object.

Use the runtime's bounded stream factory with an iterable/stream source. Keep maximum bytes, cancellation, content type and error handling explicit. A client disconnect should stop downstream work rather than leave a file read or model stream consuming resources. Once headers are sent, a later failure cannot reliably become an unrelated JSON response. TypeScript can describe StreamResult and response options, but it does not measure emitted bytes or enforce a missing upload quota. Test empty streams, early cancellation, an upstream error, a source that exceeds its limit and a HEAD request through the real HTTP path. For private binary files use the media/files response helpers with their authorization and range policies.

api.protocols() registers JSON-RPC, MCP tools/resources, Connect and tRPC handlers and publishes SSE events. Gateway routes include /rpc, /mcp, /events and /trpc/<name . MCP implements a JSON transport subset, not every MCP transport.

Protocol endpoints are local-only by default. Requests carrying proxy forwarding headers are rejected unless protocols.authorize explicitly authorizes them. Set authentication, trusted proxy rules and allowedOrigins for real deployments.
registerFetchRoutes and createFetchRoute adapt standard Fetch handlers. The adapter preserves statuses, safe end-to-end headers and streaming cancellation; it does not add authorization.

Protocol options configure origins, request bounds and authorization. The application still registers the methods/tools/resources it intends to expose. A name or schema is not an authorization boundary, and a tool call generated by a model is untrusted input. The gateway is obtained lazily and can be disabled by protocols.enabled false. Set a real request authorization callback before external exposure; origin restrictions and loopback defaults are not a user session policy. The callback request type is the gateway's Node request contract, not automatically a Fetch Request.

Use the public ZeruxProtocols type and registered handler signatures. Validate schema-bound arguments before filesystem, database or network effects and return bounded public errors. Do not forward arbitrary tool arguments into shell commands or a database executor. Test actual transport framing, wrong methods, denied origins, missing identity, oversized bodies and cancellation. Handler unit calls do not exercise the gateway boundary. Close the owning gateway and unregister dynamic resources during teardown; a static Pages export cannot host this server gateway.

Set multisite: true in configuration, then register mappings from middleware using context.multisiteRegister(hostAndPath, folder). More-specific path prefixes match first. Exact hosts take priority over wildcard hosts at equal specificity.

A mapping example.com/shop to shop resolves example.com/shop/api/health against app/shop/api/health/route.ts. Use to register a host wildcard. Unmatched hosts do not fall through into unrelated root dynamic routes when mappings are registered.
Host routing chooses an application folder. It does not replace database tenant filters, authentication, authorization or a trusted proxy configuration.

A host/path mapping selects application content; it does not select a trusted tenant automatically. Resolve the tenant from an authenticated/server-verified mapping and enforce its data scope independently. Never pass an arbitrary query field as a folder name, storage prefix or database slug just because multisite routing is enabled. The wildcard does not include the apex automatically. Host policy, routing mappings and service data isolation are three separate checks. A single runtime can share infrastructure across sites, but each database/file/cache operation must still use the appropriate verified scope.

Use the runtime's documented mapping registration with application-owned URL/folder constants. Registration is not a dynamic filesystem browser. Review folder discovery and path semantics in the actual deployed project; adding a domain does not create DNS, TLS or a reverse-proxy entry.

The public request context describes multisiteRegister; use the real context type rather than a custom object with unchecked any fields. A typecheck cannot prove an external hostname maps to the intended tenant. Test exact hosts, wildcard subdomains, unknown hosts, malformed authority, overlapping mappings and cross-tenant resource IDs. Include cache-key/asset-prefix scope in those tests. A cached response for one site must not be returned to another site simply because both hit the same route pattern. See [tenant data](tenant-data.md) for database restrictions and [server configuration](configuration-server.md) for hostname matching behavior.

The manager package @zeruxjs/db validates and routes operations. SQL adapters share @zeruxjs/db-sql-core ; the runtime package names are @zeruxjs/db-pg , @zeruxjs/db-mysql , @zeruxjs/db-sqlite and @zeruxjs/db-mongo . The SQLite source folder has a historical spelling; use its package manifest name in imports.

One connection can become the default automatically; multiple connections require a selected default. Bootstrap initializes the manager before loading application modules and strips raw DB configuration from the public runtime config. This does not make direct environment access safe to expose.

With the Zerux loader active, db resolves to the default facade and db:reporting to a named facade. These are framework virtual imports, not npm packages. Ordinary Node scripts should construct a manager through @zeruxjs/db instead.

Operations are JSON data, with explicit table, columns, conditions, ordering and limits. SQL adapters compile values into parameters and validate identifiers. Do not accept an arbitrary client-supplied operation tree as authorization: choose tables, allowed fields and tenant filters in trusted code. Facade operations Purpose --- --- select , insert , update , delete Data access createTable , alterTable , dropTable , turcunateTable Schema/table operations; the truncate method retains its historical spelling createIndex , dropIndex Index management createDb , dropDb , switchDB Database administration query A structured operation or array of operations dbAccess(slug) / native access Trusted connector-specific operations

Array queries can execute independent operations in parallel and sequence dependsOn dependencies. $ref can refer to earlier result paths. An array is not automatically a transaction. For an atomic multi-write operation, supply a real driver transaction with appropriate connection pinning; do not infer atomicity from JavaScript order.

createTenantDatabaseFacade restricts allowlisted tables and binds a server-verified tenant. It rejects unsupported query shapes rather than attempting to prove arbitrary joins safe. The migration runner needs a host implementation that provides exclusive execution and a transaction-pinned journal/operation context. See the database package guide before adoption.

Managers disconnect previously opened connectors when partial initialization fails. Call disconnect() during standalone shutdown; framework-managed managers are closed by the service lifecycle. Queries after disconnect fail closed. Error details are internal diagnostics, not safe public API payloads.

Standalone package factories are reusable outside Zerux. You own their close/disconnect calls. A framework-managed service is constructed during generation preparation and released through the service scope. Do not construct a second competing manager solely because a package is installed.

The runtime key is connector; the standalone createCacheManager key is helper. Bootstrap maps between them. With required false, a startup failure can leave cache unavailable rather than failing the whole application. Callers must handle an absent service. A timeout is not evidence that every remote resource stopped immediately.

Plugins use api.service(name). Handlers use context.services.get(name). These return undefined for unavailable/disabled services. Supply a type based on the actual configured service and narrow the value before use; a TypeScript generic does not validate runtime configuration.

Database/cache initialize before dependent managers. The scope tracks release functions and closes in reverse initialization order, collecting cleanup errors. Queue shutdown precedes its dependent data infrastructure. Startup rollback releases partially prepared resources; application code must still return cleanup for resources it starts itself.

Some optional services register HTTP routes for collectors, preferences or dashboards. Registration rejects overlapping reserved endpoints instead of silently replacing application routes. Each package has its own authentication/origin/CSRF requirements. A dashboard callback is not supplied by the framework automatically.

Private service startup settings are removed from the runtime config exposed to handlers. Managers can still contain private clients or credentials internally; do not serialize service objects. Use allowlisted status views for operations, not whole manager snapshots.

Development may prepare a replacement generation while the old handler is still valid. Scope objects must not be shared carelessly across generations. For production restarts/rolling deploys, plan connection budgets, draining and compatibility between old and new schemas/configuration.

Application cache stores computed JSON values behind a manager. HTTP cache policies tell browsers/proxies how to reuse responses. Filling Redis does not make a response cacheable, and Cache-Control public does not save a database result to Redis. Choose both policies intentionally.
Namespace keys by ownership and format

Use an application namespace plus a data-schema version. Include a trusted tenant boundary when data differs by tenant. Prefer opaque record IDs to raw email addresses or tokens. Bump the namespace when a cached data shape becomes incompatible; TTL alone may leave old readers/new writers disagreeing during rolling deployment.

The application provides loadPublicCatalogFromDatabase. It should return bounded public JSON. remember coalesces only concurrent misses in this manager process; it is not distributed election. If remote producer work is expensive, design a separate shared lease/queue mechanism or tolerate duplicate computation.

Complete the authoritative database write first. Delete or refresh affected cache keys afterwards. A database commit and cache delete are usually separate operations; plan the failure window. TTL gives a maximum stale interval only when writes/readers follow the expected key policy. Critical consistency may require an outbox/invalidation log and versioned reads rather than best-effort deletion.

Decide whether reads can fall back to the database and whether a required startup cache should block readiness. Bound fallback load so a Redis outage does not stampede the primary database. Do not silently treat a cache failure as an authorized empty result when that changes application behavior.

setMany is not necessarily atomic. Prefix clear uses literal provider namespace support and fails closed if unavailable. Redis clear uses a sweep and can race new writes; pause/quiesce writers if emptiness must be guaranteed. Avoid FLUSHDB on shared infrastructure and keep BullMQ and cache prefixes separate.

Use cached(payload, { visibility: 'public', maxAge, etag, vary }) only after ensuring the entire representation is public. Personalized/tenant-specific responses normally need private/no-store and a reviewed Vary policy. Never allow a client-controlled tenant selector to choose a public cache entry for protected data.

A private file API needs three decisions before its storage driver: how the request is authenticated, how a principal is authorized for an object, and how the object address is selected. Do not translate an arbitrary submitted storage/bucket/key into a trusted address. Resolve it from a server-owned record and tenant membership. The files manager is the byte-storage layer. The Fetch adapter preserves HTTP semantics. Your application supplies identity and policy. The example below names these host-owned functions explicitly rather than implying the framework provides an identity database.

For a standalone service, createFileManager owns configured stores and must be closed during shutdown. For a Zerux application, files startup configuration can construct the generation-owned manager; obtain it through api.service or context.services.get. Keep its storage credentials server-side.

api and files are initialized runtime resources. authenticate, resolveOwnedDocument and canAccess are application-provided implementations. Resolve ownership before handing the object to storage. Authenticate a HEAD request as carefully as a GET: metadata itself can be private.

For uploadFileRequest, choose an authorized address, set maxBytes and private visibility, and provide write authorization. The helper streams a raw body; do not label a multipart form as raw object bytes. Validate media type, quota and accepted content separately, and quarantine/scanner-check uploads when appropriate. Do not accept the destination tenant prefix or public visibility solely from the client. A signed PUT is still a capability that must be issued only after permission checks. Decide how a successful object write becomes visible in the authoritative document record, and how failed/uncommitted objects are reclaimed.

The file response can supply ETag, conditional requests and supported byte ranges. The Fetch bridge preserves these statuses and streams with cancellation. Encrypted local objects cannot offer ordinary byte ranges after authenticated decryption. Do not buffer a large file merely to convert it back into an ordinary JSON/string handler response.

Test unauthorized IDs, cross-tenant IDs, HEAD, empty/oversized uploads, declared-length mismatch, suffix ranges, client disconnect and storage failure. For S3-compatible backends also verify actual provider encryption, multipart and signing behavior. Local or injected-client checks do not prove all cloud-provider semantics.

A worker can crash after an SMTP server accepts a message but before your database records success. Retrying that job can send a duplicate. A durable queue prevents some task loss; it cannot make an external SMTP transaction exactly-once. Use a persisted message descriptor plus a shared per-message delivery record. Queue only the opaque message ID. Resolve recipients, bodies, credentials and attachments from trusted storage at delivery time.

Transition Meaning --- --- pending → claimed One worker acquires the versioned delivery record claimed → suppressed Current marketing consent forbids delivery claimed → pending A failure before SMTP begins can be retried safely claimed → sending The worker is about to contact the sender sending → sent The sender reports acceptance and state is durably recorded sending → uncertain Error, timeout, crash or expired sending lease leaves outcome ambiguous The host store must provide atomic compare-and-swap across all workers. A module-local Map or process-local mutex cannot protect a multi-server delivery record.

All four resources are application-supplied services. The send implementation must recheck marketing permission at the actual send boundary and use the saved per-email tracking choices. Register the processor only on designated worker processes with explicit concurrency.

A marketing recipient can unsubscribe between enqueue and dispatch. Recheck current consent; a preferences-store outage is not permission to send. Transactional messages have a separate purpose contract. An opted-in recipient does not automatically opt into activity tracking, and a queued job must not change the saved tracking policy.

Investigate uncertain outcomes using provider evidence, transport logs and your durable audit record. resolveUncertainEmailDelivery records the operator's verified decision; it does not safely guess an SMTP resend. Provider idempotency or an explicit outbox can help but does not justify blind retry of every unknown outcome.

BullMQ delays need persistent Redis and available workers. Set retention for job/event history and keep Redis payloads free of message content. A scheduled batch is not a whole campaign system: use the campaign planner/outbox/suppression APIs for paging and campaign ownership. Track SMTP acceptance, provider notifications and observed opens as different measurements.

Choose allowed event names, scalar properties and tenant/site ownership before mounting a collector. The analytics pipeline is opt-in and best effort. Public browser origins must bind to trusted sites, and confidential server events require authentication. An Origin header alone is not an authenticated principal.
Request identity is not user identity

Request IDs support day-scoped deduplication/correlation. Use a shared atomic reservation store to coordinate replicas. Opaque browser visitor/session IDs must be created only under the intended consent policy. Do not infer a person from an IP address, request ID or observed open pixel.

Need Query path Interpretation --- --- --- Recent event inspection Bounded raw event page A sample/page, not a global total Counts over supported dimensions Native aggregate Exact for persisted matching rows Numeric sum/average/min/max Configured materialized numeric facts Indexed-only coverage Historical numeric repair Reconciliation pages/jobs Resumable repair, not a transactional completeness proof Before comparing a chart to another system, compare its time window, tenant filter, dimensions, persisted-row coverage and ingestion loss policy.

Configure numericFields before expecting native numeric metrics. Old events are not automatically materialized. Reconciliation requires a database-enforced unique event/property constraint and a trusted execution policy. A completed pass can still miss later-arriving events; restart only through an approved administrative path when necessary.

The Reports service needs host authorization. Viewer, editor, export, sensitive-property and campaign privileges are distinct. For multiple tenants use a verified scope with a dedicated definition store. Query filtering by site does not isolate saved documents if every tenant reads one shared report definition envelope.

Keep queryMode, truncated and coverage information with every exported chart. Multi-chart exports execute separate bounded queries and are not an immutable transactional snapshot. A custom warehouse source can extend scale, but it must preserve tenant authorization and honest coverage metadata.

Analytics retention deletes are bounded administrative operations with explicit approval. They do not erase every email, suppression, external-provider or browser record. Align retention with a broader data inventory. Email open/click/download-click observations should not be labeled confirmed unique human engagement or completed downloads.

The event type checks value shapes; the server must still validate unknown browser events, consent, origins and site scope. A client must not mark its event source as trusted server data. Use the analytics package's actual summary/aggregate query types and preserve coverage/truncation metadata in the caller's result. When comparing reports, identify whether each number is a raw event page, a database-native count or an indexed numeric aggregate. Consent drops, deduplication reservations, failed writes and reconciliation windows can make those numbers differ without a chart bug. A typed result does not guarantee complete source coverage. Choose retention and deletion policy before collecting events. Check cross-site source filtering, aggregate fact updates and restart behavior with a real database. Rebuild or reconcile derived data according to its own contract rather than assuming a chart refresh repairs stored facts. See [analytics configuration](configuration-analytics.md) and [report configuration](configuration-reports.md) for the complete startup and adapter inputs.

Resolve the caller through trusted authentication and membership. A submitted tenant ID, host prefix or role string is a request claim, not proof of permission. hasTenantPermission/requireTenantPermission enforce exact explicit scopes on a previously validated principal; they do not verify that principal themselves.

createTenantDatabaseFacade receives a base database facade, tenantId, allowlisted logical-to-physical tables and an optional tenant column. It exposes only scoped select/insert/update/delete and rejects joins, unions, subqueries, cross-database routes and tenant-field changes. Construct the facade in trusted server code after checking membership. Do not accept the table mapping from the request. A narrow facade is preferable to exposing the entire database manager as a generic JSON query endpoint.

Tenant isolation also applies to cache keys, file storage prefixes, search documents, queue IDs, report definition stores and analytics sites. Enforcing a row filter while sharing an unrestricted report definition document or search index can still leak information. Review each subsystem's boundary rather than assuming one tenant helper protects the whole application.

Cross-replica compare-and-swap depends on an atomic conditional write and reliable affected-row counts. A successful SQL execution with zero updated rows is a conflict, not success. Do not replace a durable CAS adapter with a read-then-write object mutation guarded only by a local mutex.

The migration runner checks ordered IDs, checksums/drift and reverse approvals. The host must provide exclusivity and a transaction-pinned journal/operation context. A transaction name or JavaScript callback does not create database atomicity when the underlying statements use different pooled connections. Some DDL is not transactionally reversible on every engine. Review actual driver/engine capabilities, back up beforehand and stage forward-compatible changes for rolling deployments. Do not run privileged migration routes as anonymous HTTP handlers.

Test restoration on the real engine and storage layout. SQLite live backup is distinct from copying an active WAL file. Queue and email state may reference database records, so a partial restore needs a reconciliation plan. Keep an operator audit trail for administrative migrations, retention and uncertain-delivery resolution.

The caller must supply a previously authenticated and validated principal. Constructing an object that satisfies TenantPrincipal from query parameters does not authenticate it. When a site is part of the policy, require its explicit allowed scope too.

Use a restricted tenant database facade only for its supported CRUD subset. It rejects operations that could escape the allowlisted table/tenant boundary; do not bypass those restrictions by reaching the native client with request-controlled SQL. A routing/multisite mapping is separate from data authorization. Include verified tenant and data revision in cache keys and partition file/media keys or buckets deliberately. A signed file token or request ID is not universal proof of tenant ownership. Shared Redis prefixes, application IDs and atomic file writes are coordination tools, not a replacement for authorization.

Test another tenant's resource ID, an unlisted table, a modified tenant column, unauthorized metadata/list pagination and stale cache entries after permissions change. Run migration/transaction logic under the real exclusive connection owner. TypeScript interfaces cannot prove row-level constraints or that a saved report's data source remains correctly scoped.

Registries resolve dotted paths against own properties and registered resolver functions. Only scalar values are rendered; objects must be transformed intentionally. Forbidden prototype paths are rejected. Templates do not execute JavaScript expressions.

HTML escaping must be requested for HTML fields. Plain text interpolation is appropriate for email subject/text fields, not HTML markup. HTML escaping does not validate a URL, CSS token or JavaScript string embedded in another syntax. Do not put user-controlled values into dangerous HTML contexts.

renderFields accepts a bounded map of fields and per-field escape modes. It evaluates a named variable once per render snapshot, including asynchronous resolvers, so subject/HTML/text can agree. Set missing to empty, keep or error and define a maximum output budget.

Prefer api.variables() for a generation-scoped registry or create an explicit registry per application/tenant. The exported convenience singleton is process-scoped and can cross application boundaries if used carelessly. Resolvers should derive user-specific values from the supplied verified context rather than mutable globals.

The implementation bounds field counts, template lengths, variable counts and output size. These limits prevent accidental unbounded interpolation but do not authorize access to a field. Register only values the recipient is permitted to see.

ThemeMode is light, dark or system. The runtime can process returned HTML and insert configured preference behavior. This is distinct from composing React/Vue components or generating a complete design system.

zeruxjs/theme exports getThemeConfig, getThemeMode, getThemeByPrefersColor, getResolvedTheme, getThemeLabel and getThemeIcon. Server resolution can inspect request cookies and the prefers-color client hint; browser resolution can use matchMedia. Without client information, server output cannot know every user's device preference.

setTheme updates the browser document and preference cookie; it does nothing when no document exists. Treat a theme cookie as a display preference only, never identity or permission. Ensure your CSS supports the emitted classes and color-scheme behavior.

Label the control, keep keyboard focus visible and respect reduced motion. Test first paint and preference changes. If you render different client/server markup based on a theme, account for hydration consistency in the chosen renderer.

This static site uses CSS system preference plus an optional browser-local theme override. It does not execute the framework runtime at request time, and does not claim its static theme control installs the framework theme system.
A bridge is not a renderer

@zeruxjs/react, @zeruxjs/vue and @zeruxjs/zyro coordinate state and subscriptions. They do not automatically turn a Zerux HTML-string route into a React/Vue server-rendering pipeline. The host renderer owns component rendering, state serialization, client assets and hydration.

Create state per request when it includes private/user-specific data. A module singleton can accidentally share identity or cart data across requests. Browser stores can live as long as the intentionally shared application shell; route-owned subscriptions should be disposed on navigation/unmount.

createReactStore supports a pinned serverSnapshot. Supply the same shape/value through the initial hydration payload and a stable getServerSnapshot on the client. Stabilize selectors with useCallback or a module function; a selector allocating a new object on every read needs an appropriate comparator/memoization strategy. Injected useMemo/useSyncExternalStore must be real React hooks invoked within components. The adapter does not own React's component lifetime. Do not run a hook function at module top level because it has a use-style name.

createVueBindings receives actual Vue runtime functions. useStore expects an active effect scope and disposes with it. SSR mode reads a one-time snapshot and creates no live external subscription. Outside a scope, connect returns an explicit stop function. The standalone createVueRef primitive is not a native Vue ref.

Selected/combined observables retain stable snapshots. Async resources pass an AbortSignal, cancel older work and ignore stale completions. Use a subscription scope for all route-owned observers and destroy it on leave. A canceled UI request should not mutate an already-destroyed route view.

Serialize only an allowlisted public projection. Never send runtime/context/service objects or process.env to a browser. If JSON is embedded inside an HTML script payload, escape the HTML-breaking characters with a proven serializer; JSON.stringify alone does not make an arbitrary string safe inside an HTML script element. Keep the client and server snapshot consistent after sanitization.

A state change does not automatically announce itself. Author semantic buttons, tabs and panels with correct references. Dispose focus/dialog helpers on teardown and test keyboard focus after route changes. Reduced-motion behavior and screen-reader announcements belong to the user interaction design, not just state adapters.

Define a narrow public snapshot rather than serializing server context or manager options. For example, an interface describing a counter and display name is useful shared data; it must not grow to include session keys or database configuration just because those fields are available on the server. The host must serialize the same snapshot used during server rendering and supply it at hydration. TypeScript checks the shape, not whether a client received a different value or whether untrusted text was escaped for a script context. Use script-safe JSON serialization and the actual renderer's documented hydration behavior.

Render two users concurrently with different initial state and verify neither sees the other's snapshot. Dispose effects/subscriptions created during an SSR owner rather than leaving browser-style subscriptions in a long-lived server process. On the client, verify hydration, updates and unmount with the real React/Vue/Zyro integration, not only a structural fake store. A store adapter does not implement a complete SSR renderer, route transport or generic hydration engine. Keep capability statements tied to the actual library and release; choose an explicit static renderer or component integration rather than inferring one from a package name.

A server page can return a complete HTML string. Layout files are reserved by discovery, but this does not automatically compose layouts or render MDX. This documentation site uses its own shared server-side template at build time.

The monorepo includes React, Vue, ZyroJS and Zuixs packages. Check each package README and exports for current capabilities. Avoid assuming a complete hydration pipeline or framework adapter from its package name.

zeruxjs/accessibility exports bindAccessibleTabs and prefersReducedMotion. Tabs require buttons with matching aria-controls, panel IDs and aria-labelledby references. Destroy the binding on unmount. DOM globals are accessed inside browser functions, making imports safe on the server.

createVariableRegistry, variables, registerVariable and renderVariables expose configurable variable resolution. Treat escaping as a security boundary and use the correct escape mode for the output context.
Use [Zuixs utility-first styling](styling.md) for theme tokens, responsive utilities and component/Markdown recipes. The documentation site uses this compiler for its complete design.

The runtime can return complete HTML and serve browser assets, but a frontend bridge package does not install a component renderer. Keep page/server configuration separate from browser entry points and decide how initial state is serialized. A typed store bridge is useful without claiming automatic React/Vue hydration or a file-based client router. For React, inject actual hooks and keep selectors stable. For Vue, use actual effect scopes and the injected Vue runtime bindings. For standalone ZyroJS use its DOM/network entry points with explicit unmount/disposal. The observable bridge @zeruxjs/zyro has a different API from the standalone renderer.

A shared state interface can describe public initial data, but it should be an explicit subset of server state. Never serialize whole request contexts, environment objects or manager options into a script. Escape script-embedded JSON for its output context and validate user-controlled values at the server boundary before adding them to state. Browser TypeScript needs DOM libraries and a browser bundling target. Server code needs Node types and must not evaluate document/window at module import. The [TypeScript chapter](typescript.md) explains separate checking/building and the package guides show actual adapter inputs.

Render meaningful links/forms/content before adding search, copying, sharing or client state. Test the page with JavaScript disabled, keyboard navigation, narrow viewports, dark/system/light themes and reduced motion. A visible toggle is not proof that every menu/dialog/surface changes correctly. Check SSR with two different users concurrently, then hydrate the matching snapshot on the client if the chosen renderer supports it. Dispose route/component subscriptions when leaving. A local browser screenshot does not certify every assistive technology or all framework adapters; report the environments actually verified.

A reusable package owns its message identifiers, translator contexts, text domain and catalog files. The application owns the active language, which catalogs enter the browser, request isolation and persistence of user preferences. Keep those responsibilities separate so two modules can run in one site without changing each other's locale or translations. Use a stable domain such as acme-cart , rather than the host's default domain. Domain names accept letters, digits, dots, underscores and hyphens, must start with a letter/digit and are bounded to 128 characters. A domain is a translation namespace; it does not isolate untrusted package code or authorize access to user data. Install zlocale@0.0.3 for development. A package exposing integration with a host-owned translator can declare a compatible peer dependency and install it as a development dependency for TypeScript. Do not construct a mutable translator singleton when the module is imported. Type-only imports disappear from compiled JavaScript.

The example package below is called @example/cart ; replace that illustrative name with your own published package. Translation reads receive a locale-fixed Translator from the host. Passing the translator makes the same function work in a Node worker, request handler, Zyro component or another framework. Prefer stable source messages over concatenating translated fragments. Translators may need to reorder words; use positional sprintf placeholders or named interpolate values when the entire sentence needs translation. These return text, so render with text nodes or escape for the actual output context. Do not translate a URL scheme, permission identifier, database key or arbitrary HTML template as if it were display text.
Publish one catalog module per locale and domain

The context separator in the TypeScript string above is the actual U+0004 escape. Include translator comments in source/review material to explain ambiguous wording. Plural categories follow native CLDR: Arabic/Russian need different categories from English. other is always required. Missing categories fall back to other ; a missing catalog/message falls back to source text. Use satisfies Catalog for authoring feedback and defineCatalog(unknown) when accepting runtime data. The registry/loader validates and freezes catalogs even if the source was already type-checked. TypeScript does not validate a downloaded JSON response.

This is an excerpt, not a complete release manifest. Add the package's own version, license and build settings. ^0.0.3 intentionally accepts only that patch line under npm's 0.0.x rules; review later versions before broadening the range. Only declare sideEffects: false if it is true for your entire package. Do not re-export every locale from the main entry. Hosts can then omit unused locales or split explicit dynamic imports into locale chunks. No extraction CLI, PO/MO parser, Jed converter or automatic bundler integration is supplied by zlocale 0.0.3; produce the documented catalog shape in your own build pipeline.
Let the application load the catalog

A server can preload all hot domains/locales once per runtime generation. A browser can import only the selected locale's required domains. In both cases cartQuantity(i18n.forLocale('fr'), 2) reads memory only. Do not build an import path from a query parameter, cookie or locale header. The allowlisted manifest maps input choices to known files. Coordinate maxCatalogs with the number of locales times installed domains. Multiple packages using the same domain can overwrite each other's translations when replacement is enabled. Give each package a unique domain and have one host owner decide replacement/version policy. Package source fallbacks remain usable before optional translations load.
Register a ZeruxJS plugin without owning the site's language

The site wraps this registration from its own discovered plugin, supplies its request-locale resolver and installs the catalogs before serving. For the named middleware in the site guide, call registerCart(api, translatorFor, ['site.language']) after registering that middleware. The module passes through the host-selected middleware names instead of assuming a global language policy. The package should not independently parse cookies, change a global locale, register a competing language preference or assume api.service('i18n') exists. The framework's managed service names do not include zlocale in this release. If a module adds loaders, subscriptions or request-context owners, put lifecycle ownership in the host's generation/worker setup. Plugin registration is not an arbitrary returned-disposer lifecycle. A package with only message functions and immutable catalog data needs no background worker.

For reactive browser text, the host creates createZyroI18n(i18n, signal) from zlocale/zyro . Its return value implements Translator , so the same package functions can receive it. Read those functions inside reactive children/effects; a string calculated once outside an effect will not update itself. For SSR or email/jobs, pass i18n.forLocale(selectedLocale) directly. Do not import zlocale/node into browser code. Do not instantiate another Zyro runtime in the translation package. Framework-neutral message functions keep the translation data usable across all of these hosts.

Before publishing the module, pack it and inspect that each public locale export resolves from an isolated install. Check missing messages, explicit domains/contexts, intentional empty translations, CLDR counts, HTML-like text and unsupported locale choices. Test two concurrent server requests with different languages and a rapid browser language switch. Confirm that importing the main entry neither starts an application nor imports every locale. Changing a source message/context/domain changes its lookup key; ship matching catalog updates. Adding translations does not justify changing another package's active language. Document catalog size, supported locales and whether a module's browser bundle actually includes its locale chunks. See [site language settings](localization-site-settings.md) for the application's side of this contract.

Zuixs is the ecosystem's utility-first styling compiler. It generates CSS from template classes and reusable utility compositions; it does not require a browser styling runtime. The documentation and ecosystem homepage use it for their entire design. The output is still a stylesheet: browsers use that generated CSS to render utility classes and component selectors. Use the current workspace implementation when developing in this repository. An installed public release only contains the functionality published with that release. These examples describe the current source implementation.

Create zuix.config.mjs in your application: Use theme tokens across templates. Arbitrary values such as ui-p-[13px] and properties such as ui-[scroll-margin-top:96px] cover precise application needs without adding one-off compiler code. Arbitrary values are restricted: declaration escapes, executable CSS and URL-loading values are rejected. Values use underscores for spaces. Prefixes belong on the utility name; an important prefixed utility is ui-!hidden .

Base utilities are emitted before responsive variants. Named breakpoints follow increasing min-width order, so larger layouts override smaller ones independently of class attribute order. Keep custom breakpoint units consistent.

Recipes apply ordinary utilities to reusable selectors. They are useful for generated Markdown, dialog states, pseudo-elements and components whose structure should remain readable. Every application is validated; unknown tokens fail compilation. Use base utility tokens in apply , and put states such as :hover in the selector. Add media , supports or container conditions for conditional recipes. Combined conditions nest in that order. Recipes preserve declaration order and importance, and appear before scanned template utilities. Normal CSS specificity still applies: a more specific component selector can override a single utility class. Recipe selectors are trusted developer configuration, never visitor input. Recipes are always emitted, including those used by content created later in the browser; keep them focused because they are not removed by the template scanner.

The package exposes the zuix command after installation. From an application directory: Link the generated stylesheet from your HTML. For programmatic integration, use createZuix(config).generate(classTokens) or the Node build API documented in the package README. The repository's site pipeline generates Zuixs CSS and then uses the TypeScript package's esbuild wrapper to minify production CSS and JavaScript; Zuixs's minify option alone primarily controls output formatting. For this repository, run npm run dev or npm run build from pages/ . Tooling workspaces are compiled first from the checkout. Change template classes, zuix.config.mjs or zuix.recipes.mjs ; do not edit generated stylesheet files. The combined development server rebuilds and reloads the browser after source changes. Production exports contain complete HTML and styles and work without JavaScript.

A normal Zerux application ships compiled .zerux/build output, package dependencies, Node and a process runner. This documentation site ships only dist static files. Do not deploy source secrets or a repository checkout as public assets.

Run zerux build from the application directory and a separate TypeScript check. Exercise the built start path, not only the development handler. Keep a lockfile and choose supported runtime/driver versions. A transpile succeeding does not establish types, authorization or service connectivity.

- Configure allowed hosts and trusted proxy handling at the edge. - Authenticate and authorize sensitive routes, including protocol and service endpoints. - Use secure cookies, origin/CSRF checks for unsafe cookie-authenticated methods, and a suitable CSP. - Bound bodies, streams, query fields and outbound calls. - Keep public assets public and private storage outside web roots. Global application middleware is not a universal perimeter: protocol/public handling precedes it. Review each endpoint's explicit authorization contract.

Use shared durable stores where restart survival and multi-instance coordination matter. Treat memory cache/token stores/local indexes as process-owned. Queue processors must be idempotent; SMTP ambiguity needs an uncertain state and reconciliation. Verify real Redis/database/object-provider behavior, not only injected test doubles.

Return cleanup from startup workers and close standalone managers. Plan graceful request draining and maximum shutdown duration. Ensure rolling deployments share required verification keys and compatible data schemas. Test failed startup and rollback, not only the happy path.

Define health/readiness checks, sanitized logs, internal metrics, backups and restoration drills. Protect debugging ports and dashboards. Keep retention, consent, unsubscribe and deletion policies separate from analytics convenience. Review dependency advisories again at release time; a previous clean audit is not permanent evidence.
Start is not using the expected build

Run zerux build in the actual application directory, then start from that directory with dependencies installed. The current resolver can fall back to source configuration when a build manifest is absent; check for a valid staged manifest rather than inferring compiled execution from a running process. A docs static export is not a framework server build. Check build logs and configured output/source paths; do not remove a last good build as the first debugging step.

Check filename conventions and method exports, then routePath/path overrides and dynamic segments. Verify the effective internal pathname after multisite rewriting. A public asset or protocol endpoint can be handled before file-route dispatch. Avoid overlapping plugin/service patterns.
Middleware did not protect an endpoint

Global application middleware does not wrap every earlier protocol/public path. Protect protocols with gateway authorization and keep confidential files out of public. Optional service dashboards have explicit host authorization and often CSRF requirements.
A Fetch handler sees an empty body

A stream may already have been consumed by the buffered parser. Register with registerFetchRoutes, or export meta.streamBody alongside createFetchRoute in the file module. Do not combine two readers for the same upload.

Candidate builds activate only after preparation succeeds. Inspect reload errors and worker startup/cleanup failures; the old successful generation may intentionally remain active. Fix the candidate error, then let a new build activate.

Memory caches, token/revocation registries, hook state, local search snapshots and local media are not automatically shared. Use an appropriate authoritative shared store. A cache remember Promise, atomic filesystem rename or local revision counter is not a distributed lock.

Check whether a query uses raw samples, native persisted-row counts or indexed numeric facts. Check dropped events, consent, request-ID reservations and reconciliation status. Tracking requests can be caused by scanners/proxies. Do not compare these measures as though they were identical unique-user counts.

BullMQ delivery is at-least-once. Use durable idempotency and compare-and-swap state. An SMTP timeout may occur after provider acceptance; reconcile uncertain state rather than automatically replaying a possibly delivered message.

Use exact manifest names and public export paths. db virtual imports require the framework loader. CommonJS require hooks do not install ESM loaders. Browser-only functions still require a DOM even when server imports are safe.

Run the separate checker and inspect the installed declaration/export path. The root configuration's index signature permits application extensions, so a misspelled top-level field may not cause a useful error; check the nested service shape. A config module accepted by the compiler can still be shadowed by a higher-priority file or read before additional environment files are loaded. Confirm the exact consumer. The docs static builder reads documentation metadata and never boots database/cache services. Standalone factories do not automatically read zerux.config.js. Browser bundles must use browser entry points; adding DOM types to a server file does not make document exist in Node.

Record the package/version, public import, startup command, owning directory, relevant config keys and redacted error category. Include a minimal input and the expected versus actual behavior. Never paste environment values, cookies, bearer tokens or raw customer payloads into an issue. Reproduce one layer at a time: validate input, initialize the adapter, perform a real operation, check ownership/shutdown, then integrate the route. If only production fails, compare the built file layout, dependency set, process identity, host/proxy headers and available environment keys. Preserve the last known-good artifact while investigating a candidate failure.

The ecosystem is at an early 0.0.x stage. Review actual exports and behavioral changes rather than assuming stability from a package name. Keep related workspace versions aligned and select a new unused package version for each release.

Current utility names include zclivo, zforge, zhost, zlook and ztrial. Old draft references can contain zcli, z-dev, zsrv, zwatch or zeyro. Use installed manifests and current source as the authority. The PostgreSQL package is @zeruxjs/db-pg and the SQLite package is @zeruxjs/db-sqlite even when an old source folder has a historical typo.

Compile and separately typecheck a representative application. Exercise error paths, middleware order, streamed uploads, worker cleanup and the built start path. A local package symlink can hide missing tarball files, so inspect the actual release artifact when validating package changes.

Schema changes, cache prefixes, serialized search snapshots, message-delivery state and key-ring rotation need explicit migration plans. Preserve old verification keys while old encrypted links remain valid. Do not rotate password/session salts as an ordinary deploy without understanding account/session compatibility.

Coordinate old/new database schemas and control-plane document versions. Keep required shared stores available across replicas. Avoid running a migration runner concurrently without exclusive ownership, and designate which processes own queue workers.

Freeze the current package reference snapshot before bumping packages, pin implementation links to a release ref, and create the next content version. Archived docs must not silently read the newest workspace manifest. Explain changed behavior and migration steps in the guide where the API is used.

Check configuration and package examples against the actual target release declarations. A new workspace API does not exist in a previously installed registry version. Run the checker against public imports and the production build; do not use internal source imports to hide an export-map change. Review runtime-consumed configuration separately from type-only compatibility fields. Changes to a cache adapter, default connection, session key/salt, report store or queue prefix can change persisted state and cross-instance behavior even when the TypeScript code still compiles. Plan migration and rollback for that state before deploying code.

Freeze the prior release's reference snapshot and source ref before changing the live docs version. Keep old public guide routes where practical, and update raw Markdown alternatives, package claims and related links with the same release. An archived manifest paired with newer authored examples can misrepresent compatibility; review both. Verify normal startup, required-service failure, optional-service degradation, a request, a job/stream if used, and shutdown on the upgraded deployment. Keep bounded backups and test restoration rather than assuming rolling back a package reverses a data migration or encrypted-token change.

zerux build compiles routes, controllers, plugins and public assets into .zerux/build. A successful build replaces the prior output; failed compilation leaves the last good build. zerux start consumes the build manifest when it exists. The current resolver can fall back to source configuration when no manifest exists, so verify your deployment actually contains a valid build; start alone is not proof of compiled execution. Run typechecking separately.

In apps/zerux-docs, npm run build renders every documentation route into dist/zeruxjs/<route /index.html, along with CSS, search data and a 404 page. It uses no browser hydration and needs no runtime server on the deployment host.

For documentation, serve directory index.html files and use dist/404.html as the missing-page response. Do not configure an SPA fallback: every page is already rendered. For framework applications, configure TLS, application domains, process restarts and service credentials at the host.

Start from the committed application manifest and lockfile, install its dependencies, run a separate typecheck and build the production application. The server compiler is not the docs static exporter; deploy the artifact appropriate to the app you are actually hosting. Keep source, runtime output, private uploads and configuration secrets in distinct locations. Use a supported Node runtime for the chosen adapters. Native SQLite or optional binary tooling can behave differently on a clean machine and operating system, so verify the installed production dependency set rather than relying on a workspace symlink or development cache.

Set deployment environment values through the process/secret store and load one authoritative zerux.config file. Check database, cache, queue and email readiness policies before serving traffic. A compiler build does not prove the external services are reachable with the deployment identity. TypeScript configuration can use satisfies ZeruxConfig and narrower service types, but the generated JavaScript still reads environment values at runtime. Additional structure.env loading order differs from direct imports/builds. Avoid copying private environment files into a static public folder to make a missing value disappear.

Configure DNS, TLS, host forwarding and allowedDomains consistently. Keep internal developer tools and protected dashboards behind explicit application authorization/network policy. Run with filesystem permissions limited to required output/storage paths; a local development proxy is not automatically the production security boundary. Test graceful shutdown while requests, streams and workers are active. Verify owned connections close and pending jobs follow their delivery/idempotency policy. Establish backups and a tested restore path for persistent data, not only a source-code rollback.

The repository docs build renders HTML and raw Markdown, minifies production HTML/CSS/JS and validates links/content hashes. GitHub Pages deploys static files, so no database/cache runtime starts there. The zerux.config documentation namespace configures that exporter only. See the repository SITE_DEPLOYMENT.md for the shared root and per-site mounts.
Use context.logger or the exported Logger/logger APIs. Never log credentials, cookies, personal tokens or complete environment objects. Keep request state isolated and sanitize user-provided fields.

api.getLoadStatus(windowMs) and runtime.getLoadStatus(windowMs) report bounded request counts, status families, HTTP versions, concurrency and latency. No public metrics endpoint is served automatically; authorize any route you add.

Validate hosts and origins, set request and stream limits, confirm cleanup behavior, review dependency advisories and exercise authentication failures. A successful build does not certify production security.

If start cannot find its build, run zerux build in the application directory. For failed development reloads, inspect dev.json reload status and logs; the last good generation may still be active. Placeholder scaffolders print help rather than generating files.

Use runtime load metrics for the current application process, structured logs for diagnostic events and analytics for product/event reporting. These are not interchangeable. An analytics outage should not hide a service-startup error, and a low average latency does not prove the absence of failing or abandoned requests. Protect internal diagnostics with application middleware/host policy before exposing them; this example only demonstrates the API shape. A public endpoint must not leak request identities, database credentials or filesystem paths. The window argument selects the relevant load observation interval, not a cross-instance metrics query.

Infer the returned shape with ReturnType from the installed API or use the framework's exported metrics types. Missing/degraded/closed service states have different meanings. A type annotation does not prove an external adapter is healthy; include a bounded real readiness check where needed without turning it into an expensive action on every request. Record duration and a correlation identifier, but avoid complete request bodies, cookies, tokens and raw AI/mail content. When investigating errors, distinguish expected denied/invalid requests from backend faults. Report sampling/truncation and process scope so operators do not read an incomplete metric as a deployment-wide total.

Test a slow request, an error, a cancelled stream and service degradation. Compare development with production output and the actual reverse proxy. Add external monitoring/export with deliberate authentication and retention; an in-process metrics snapshot is not a durable monitoring backend or an automatic alerting system.

A queue service manages named BullMQ queues. Producers add small job payloads; designated worker processes execute processors. Do not register processors on every web replica unless that deployment is intentional.

BullMQ jobs are at-least-once. Make handlers idempotent through authoritative storage, not only a job ID. Producers fail quickly during Redis outages; worker connections use the blocking-operation retry policy. Delay/repeat schedules need live workers and durable Redis persistence.

Store identifiers rather than bodies, recipients, credentials or personal data in Redis. Queue cleanup precedes cache/database cleanup. Keep BullMQ prefix separate from cache prefixes and never use ioredis keyPrefix. Use noeviction and a persistence policy appropriate to recovery needs.

Operations are denied without administration.authorize. The optional dashboard additionally requires host session authentication and CSRF callbacks. Inspect returns bounded redacted summaries; raw queue job APIs can reveal private data and are trusted server-only. Queue pause is global; worker pause affects one process.

The durable email processor uses a host-supplied atomic CAS record and treats sending failures/expired sending leases as uncertain. QueueEvents is a bounded stream, not a permanent audit trail. Persist operational events separately when retention matters and reconcile uncertain sends with provider evidence.

Use the browser entry point for public, static documentation routes: Install once per document. The controller waits for hover or keyboard focus, submits speculation prefetch rules when supported, and otherwise uses link prefetch hints. It never prerenders or executes a destination page. Offline, slow connections and Save-Data suppress new hints. Use strategy: 'link' for a restrictive inline-script CSP, or supply an allowed nonce for speculation rules. Without a DOM the installer returns a disabled controller.
