Use locale-fixed views and identical public catalogs/timezone for deterministic server/client formatting. This is not a hydration engine.

Native Intl instances are reused in a bounded LRU cache. Date/time formatting defaults to UTC rather than the server's local timezone; override it deliberately for a user's display timezone. Actual text can vary with host ICU/CLDR data. This package does not ship polyfills or a timezone database. Translations and interpolation return plain strings. Zyro text children escape DOM text. For server-rendered HTML text/quoted attributes, use escapeHtml ; validate URL contexts separately. Never insert a translated string using innerHTML. interpolate accepts named own string/finite-number values. sprintf supports strings, integers, floats, positional arguments and precision; it does not implement the complete PHP format grammar. Neither function evaluates code or executes message instructions.

Public Catalog , CatalogLimits , Message , PluralCategory , I18nOptions , Translator and I18n types describe the integration. defineCatalog(unknown) validates runtime JSON-shaped data and returns an immutable catalog. TypeScript alone is not validation. Own accessors, symbol properties, unsupported plural categories and nonplain objects are rejected. Defaults are 64 registered catalogs, 20,000 messages per catalog, 16,384 characters per string, a 4 MiB UTF-8 text budget per catalog, and 64 formatter-cache entries. Loader defaults are 32 cached catalogs, 16 in-flight loads and preload concurrency 4. Applications may choose explicit bounded limits. All API instances belong to the host application; no import-time singleton locale is shared across users. Package qualification covers translation fallback, CLDR plurals, adversarial catalogs, atomic updates, bounded/single-flight loading, concurrent Node contexts, real Zyro signal subscriptions, browser bundling and packed-package consumers. Verify your actual browsers, language catalogs, ICU deployment, response caching and application lifecycle before production adoption.

Version 0.0.2 adds typed serializeCatalogs(catalogs, options?) and parseCatalogs(text, options?) . Serialize an explicit public locale/domain subset on the server and hydrate it before the first browser render. This avoids refetching catalogs already used for SSR. The versioned envelope escapes HTML delimiters and Unicode line separators, rejects duplicate locale/domain pairs and unsupported versions, and returns deeply frozen validated catalogs. Only expose public translations: escaping does not make confidential messages public-safe. Payloads default to at most 64 catalogs and 8 MiB UTF-8; SnapshotOptions lets you configure maxCatalogs , maxBytes , and per-catalog limits . HTML escaping here is specifically for a JSON data block, not an attribute, URL or executable script. Match locale, timezone and fallback settings across server and browser to avoid hydration differences.

Version 0.0.3 provides createLocaleController and the TypeScript types LocaleController , LocaleControllerOptions and LocaleLoader . Supply the application-owned i18n , its bounded catalog loader, an explicit locale allowlist and required domains. Rapid selections are last-selection-wins: a slower earlier locale cannot overwrite the latest one. All required catalogs must load, validate and match their requested locale/domain keys before installation. The old locale stays active while loading. A current failure rejects; superseded, cancelled or disposed work resolves false . cancel() ignores pending results without cancelling shared loader imports. Unsupported locale selections reject before loading. Catalog keys use the selected BCP-47 base name; explicitly preload parent/fallback catalogs if the application needs them. Supported locales are bounded to 128 and domains to 32. Subscriber callbacks should not throw: registration and locale changes notify separately, and a thrown subscriber can follow a committed registry update. This controller changes an application-owned locale, never a shared server request locale; use zlocale/node for request isolation.

Each version has a flat directory of Markdown files in apps/zerux-docs/src/docs/<version /. A file starts with a JSON metadata block delimited by --- lines, followed by ordinary Markdown. JSON makes metadata validation explicit and avoids ambiguous YAML coercions. The filename determines the stable slug. Include package for a package guide, for example @zeruxjs/cache. Exactly one authored guide may claim a package for a version.

Explain when to use a feature, show a minimal complete example, define ownership and cleanup, cover errors/constraints, and link the implementation. Use real public imports. Distinguish standalone package configuration from framework startup configuration. Define application-supplied callbacks instead of presenting them as built-ins.

Use level-two headings for primary sections and level-three for subsections. Stable unique heading slugs become table-of-contents links. Link to another page as [label](routing.md), including a heading fragment if necessary. Fenced code accepts a language and an optional title attribute for a filename. Tables, lists, blockquotes and inline code use standard Markdown. Raw HTML is escaped; do not embed script tags or executable MDX.

Run npm run build in apps/zerux-docs. The build rejects missing metadata, unknown sections, broken source references, duplicate routes/IDs, invalid related pages, missing static assets and broken local links/anchors. It checks search entries too, and promotes the new output only after validation. npm run check rechecks an existing export.

Before bumping live packages, run npm run snapshot -- <old-version . Commit the reference.snapshot.json file, mark that version reference as snapshot in src/site.config.mjs, and pin its ref to a Git commit/tag. Add the new version and copy/review its Markdown directory, then set site.latest. Version switching keeps the current slug when it exists or falls back to introduction. Do not leave old documentation reading current manifests: that silently changes archived API contracts. The live reference builder requires the framework version to match the live docs version; independently released ecosystem packages keep their own versions.

Keep reference links and examples synchronized with code. State implementation boundaries without claiming a whole framework ecosystem from a package name. Security, durability, authorization and query coverage should be described at the relevant API boundary, not only in a generic disclaimer. Review both desktop and mobile output and exercise keyboard navigation when changing presentation.

Every runtime-service guide should identify the exact zerux.config key, installation prerequisites, JavaScript/default-export setup, a TypeScript satisfies example, meaningful values/defaults, dependencies and failure policy. Typecheck self-contained snippets, but label host-provided callbacks and infrastructure prerequisites separately. A passing compiler does not send SMTP, create a database schema or certify Redis behavior. Keep source-backed option tables current when declarations change. Tables list declared values, not automatic runtime consumption; nested/inherited types retain their own contracts. Include a realistic example and explain ownership instead of relying only on an exhaustive schema dump.

Build from the application directory. Verify generated HTML, raw Markdown alternatives, source links, cross-page anchors, package coverage, navigation and search. Check a narrow viewport and long option/code tables, keyboard interactions, reduced motion and JavaScript-disabled reading.
